name: Saint Pius X
history: Giuseppe Sarto, the son of a village postman, was a parish priest for years before becoming bishop of Mantua, Patriarch of Venice and, in 1903, pope. His motto was to restore all things in Christ. He encouraged frequent Communion, allowed children to receive it from the age of reason, and renewed sacred music.
life: Giuseppe Sarto was born at Riese in the Veneto, one of ten children of a poor family. After ordination in 1858 he served as a curate and then a parish priest, teaching the catechism himself and caring for the sick in a cholera outbreak. He became bishop of Mantua in 1884 and Patriarch of Venice in 1893, and remained simple in his habits. Elected pope in 1903, he took as his programme Saint Paul’s words, to restore all things in Christ. He urged the faithful to receive Communion often, even daily, and in 1910 ruled that children could make their First Communion once they reached the age of reason. He promoted Gregorian chant, reformed the breviary, began the first Code of Canon Law and defended the faith against the errors of his day. He died in August 1914, weeks after the outbreak of the First World War, which he had dreaded. Pius XII canonised him in 1954.
prayerTo: Saint Pius, you were a parish priest at heart and wished to bring everyone, even little children, close to Christ in the Eucharist. Pray for children preparing for their First Communion, for catechists and parents, and for me, that I may receive our Lord often and worthily. Amen.
penance: Go to Mass and receive Communion today if you can, and pray for children preparing for their First Communion this year.
meditation: Holy Communion, he taught, is the shortest and surest way to heaven. How do you prepare to receive it, and how do you give thanks afterwards?
